newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana confirms Libyan plane landed in Accra.
newsitem.headline: Ghana confirms Libyan plane landed in Accra.

text.p: A Libyan plane flew an official delegation to Ghana on Tuesday despite a U.N. embargo on Libya's international flights, a Ghanaian government minister said on Wednesday.

"The Libyan delegation was here briefly to hold consultations on the impending ministerial conference of the OAU (Organisation of African Unity)," deputy foreign minister Mohamed Chambas told Reuters.
"They came in their own plane and we held a brief meeting and they went back. Tomorrow we are going to brief Security Council ambassadors (in Ghana) on the whole affair," he added.
OAU ministers are due to meet in Tripoli later this month.

Chambas did not identify the Libyan officials on the trip, but a Libyan delegation led by Foreign Minister Omar Mustafa al-Montasser has been touring West Africa in recent days. It was last known to be in Zaire on Tuesday.

Tripoli said on Wednesday a Libyan aircraft had flown a Libyan foreign ministry delegation to Accra despite a 1992 United Nations ban on its international flights because of Libya's alleged support of terrorism.
The official Libyan news agency JANA, monitored in Tunis, said an adviser to President Jerry Rawlings and a Ghanaian foreign ministry official greeted the delegation at the airport.

Rawlings who first seized power as a radical young air force officer has had close ties with Libya's revolutionary leader Muammar Gaddafi. Rawlings was re-elected last month for a second four-year term as civilian head of state.
An airport source witnessed the visit of the Libyans.
"A Libyan Boeing 727 arrived here at 8.39 p.m. (2039 GMT) yesterday and left at 11 p.m.," he said, adding that officials later removed records of the flight.
